newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh central bank protests 'insult' of chief.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh central bank protests 'insult' of chief.

text.p: Hundreds of employees from the Bangladesh central bank held a noisy protest on Tuesday against comments made by two top industrialists that allegedly insulted bank Governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, officials said.

They said the protesters condemned the "verbal insult" during a heated exchange of words on Sunday between the governor and chairman and deputy chairman of Beximco industries, Sohel Rahman and Salman Rahman.
"We won't stop demanding punishment for the culprits," one employee from Bangladesh Bank, the central bank, said during the protest inside the bank.
Local newspapers on Tuesday reported that the Rahman brothers "misbehaved" over the governor's reported move to halt an extension of fresh credit to Beximco.
The central bank says the group has defaulted on previous borrowings.
Beximco has denied the allegations that have made headlines in all Bangladeshi newspapers.
The company accused the central bank of leaking malicious information about the Beximco group of companies to the press.
Salman Rahman has not directly commented on the issues but said on Tuesday that his companies had been targeted by Bangladesh Bank.

"We only wanted to know from the governor how we could do business if our companies fall victim to discriminatory action of the central bank. The law should be applied equally for all," he told Reuters.

"The objective of the meeting was to convey to the Bangladesh Bank our concern regarding discrimination to Beximco in certain cases and the serious consequences for some Beximco companies in terms of production, export and employment if such discrimination continues."
He denied insulting the governor during the meeting on Sunday.
Central Bank sources said the Beximco group of companies owed 17 commercial banks more than 10 billion taka in outstanding loans.
The country's bank company act prohibits sanctioning of bank credit to any loan defaulter.
The Beximco group has 10 listed companies out of 31 companies on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), with capitalisation of 12.41 billion taka on Tuesday.
This accounted for 14.17 percent of the DSE's total capitalisation, said Abul Kalam Majumdar, the Corporate finance manager of the Group.
